solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: A fine female, fit and friendly

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
fit, in the sense of capable, means able

explanation.surface: A fine young woman described as fit and friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' reads as the slang compliment, but it means capable here.
explanation.definitionFit: An affable person is genial and pleasant to talk to, a close synonym.

clue.text: Dismay about return of Queen outfit

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: to dismay is to appal

indicators.note: return of means the abbreviation for Queen is read backwards

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone dismayed at the Queen's outfit being sent back.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel means clothing, as does an outfit.

clue.text: Woods warning by second tees

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shouted warning
tees are letters T, written Ts

explanation.surface: A golfer's warning shout beside the second tee.
explanation.walkthrough: The golf picture makes woods look like clubs; it is trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Forests are large areas of trees, much the same as woods.

clue.text: Having a position when in sack

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the sack is slang for bed
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Being located somewhere while lying in a sack.
explanation.definitionFit: Based means stationed or located somewhere, so having a position there.

clue.text: Insect found in say, border plant

parts.note: say, for example, abbreviates to eg

indicators.note: found in means the insect sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: a line is a boundary or border
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: An insect discovered in a garden border plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'border plant' reads as one phrase, but 'border' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is the sweetbriar, a wild rose plant.

clue.text: A clot is treated for patient

indicators.note: treated suggests something worked over or processed, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A blood clot is being treated, and the person bearing it is patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' rearranges A CLOT IS; 'for' links to the definition, which reads as a hospital noun but is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stoical endures hardship calmly without complaint, which is what patient can mean.

clue.text: Crack setter often leaves vague enigmas initially

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of each word

explanation.surface: The setter often leaves riddles too vague to crack.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack a puzzle is to solve it, a synonym.

clue.text: Sitting with old boy on hobby-horse

indicators.note: on in a down clue means placed above, so this piece comes first

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a sitting, of a court or parliament, is a session

explanation.surface: Someone sitting with an old schoolmate on a toy horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' in a down clue means placed above. 'Hobby-horse' looks like a toy but means a pet subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobby-horse is a pet subject someone keeps returning to, which is an obsession.

clue.text: Reportedly catch a severe infection

indicators.note: reportedly means we take the sound of the words as spoken

parts.note: to catch a criminal is to collar them, followed by a

explanation.surface: It is said you can catch a serious infection.
explanation.definitionFit: Cholera is a serious bacterial infection of the intestines.

clue.text: Unruly girl's behind holding unruly youth up

indicators.note: holding means containing, so a piece sits inside

parts.note: behind, as in behind schedule, means late

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth rebel

explanation.surface: A rowdy girl's bottom holding up a delinquent youth.
explanation.walkthrough: A ladette is a British term for a brash, hard-drinking young woman; a Ted was a 1950s Teddy boy.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladette is a young woman who behaves boisterously, a female counterpart of a lad.

clue.text: Certain to turn over in intimate examination

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: an intimate friend is a pal

indicators.note: to turn over asks for the word for certain to be read backwards

parts.note: certain means sure

explanation.surface: Something sure to be turned over during a close medical examination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intimate' looks like an adjective qualifying examination, but it is the noun for a close friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A perusal is a careful reading or inspection, so an examination of something.

clue.text: Girl expressed pleasure vocally, getting caught

parts.note: a lass is a girl, especially in northern Britain

indicators.note: vocally means we hear the word rather than see it spelt

parts.note: to express pleasure is to say ooh, so oohed

explanation.surface: A girl squealed with delight on being caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vocally' says OOHED is heard, and it sounds like OED, which ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassoed means caught with a looped rope, as a cowboy catches cattle.

clue.text: Through decree nisi, I left moving house

indicators.note: moving signals that the remaining letters are shifted into a new order
left means departed, so this letter is taken out of the fodder

explanation.surface: After a divorce decree, someone has left and is moving house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I left' removes one I from DECREE NISI, and 'moving' rearranges the rest. A decree nisi is the provisional order in an English divorce.
explanation.definitionFit: A residence is the place where someone lives, a formal word for a home.

clue.text: Got a whiff of fish

definitions.meaning: detected by nose; the British past tense of the verb to smell
a small silvery food fish related to the salmon

explanation.definitionFit: Smelt is a British past tense of smell, and also the name of a small fish.

clue.text: Composer's final character in record

indicators.note: in tells us the letter is placed inside the word for record

parts.note: a list is a written record of items
the final character of the alphabet is Z

explanation.surface: A composer's last note is in the record books.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Composer is just 'is' linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian Romantic composer and virtuoso pianist.

clue.text: Ship new craft over on south dock

indicators.note: over means the pieces are turned and read backwards

parts.note: a craft is a skill or art
a dock is in a port

explanation.surface: A ship, a new craft, comes in to dock in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses N and ART to TRAN; 'on' joins S and PORT.
explanation.definitionFit: To ship goods is to transport them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: One 'rug' filling void is lifeless

indicators.note: filling means these pieces go into the word for void

parts.note: void, meaning empty and senseless, gives inane
one is the Roman numeral I
a rug is a mat

explanation.surface: A single rug filling an empty room makes it feel lifeless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inanimate has no life, like a stone or a chair.

clue.text: One's a hard case or hard top, possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters may be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A tough person, or perhaps a hard-topped car.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's means 'has': an arthropod has a hard exoskeleton.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthropods, such as insects and crabs, are creatures with a hard outer shell.

clue.text: Will try to accept pet name

indicators.note: to accept means to take something in, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: to try is to test
a pet animal is tame

explanation.surface: Someone will try to get a pet's name accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like the verb starting the sentence, but it is the noun, the legal document.
explanation.definitionFit: A last will and testament is the document setting out what happens to an estate after death.

clue.text: Contracting this tautens terribly

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Catching this disease makes your muscles stiffen dreadfully.
explanation.walkthrough: Lockjaw makes muscles go rigid, so the whole clue describes the disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetanus, also called lockjaw, causes painful stiffening of the muscles.

clue.text: More like dressing, or less dressed?

definitions.meaning: more like a sauce, the culinary dressing
more risqué, wearing less, as in a saucy picture

explanation.definitionFit: Saucier means more like a sauce, and also cheekier or racier, as with scanty clothing.

clue.text: Smells bit of fish turning, fish oddly

indicators.note: turning means the word for a bit of fish is read backwards

parts.note: a fin is a part of a fish

indicators.note: oddly picks the odd-numbered letters of the second fish

explanation.surface: Stinks from fish going off, fish that smell odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses FIN to NIF; 'oddly' picks F and S from FISH. NIFF is British slang for a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Niffs is British slang for unpleasant odours, so it means smells as a noun.

clue.text: Twisting former husband in brief affair

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a fling is a short romance
an ex is a former spouse

explanation.surface: Wrestling with an ex-husband in a short-lived romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Flexing means bending or twisting, as a muscle or a rod.

clue.text: End of italics slanted and unnatural

indicators.note: end of takes the last letter of italics

parts.note: slanted means tilted

explanation.surface: Italic type that slopes looks forced and unnatural.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilted speech or writing is stiff and forced, so unnatural.

clue.text: Tory leader's 'Cuddles for hooligans'

indicators.note: a leader is the first, so the first letter of Tory is taken

parts.note: cuddles are hugs

explanation.surface: A Conservative leader's slogan proposing cuddles for young yobs.
explanation.walkthrough: This recalls the 'hug a hoodie' jibe at a Tory leader; a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Thugs are violent ruffians, much the same as hooligans.

clue.text: Plain site with green eruption

indicators.note: an eruption throws things up in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grassy site where a volcanic eruption took place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eruption' rearranges SITE and GREEN; 'with' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serengeti is a vast grassland plain in Tanzania and Kenya.

clue.text: Sabbath want to get fashionable

parts.note: to want is to wish

explanation.surface: Wanting the Sabbath to become stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Swish is informal British for smart or posh, so fashionable.

clue.text: Thinner veil revealing cheek

indicators.note: revealing means part of the words is shown, the letters inside them

explanation.surface: A thinner veil that shows off a cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve means audacity or impudence, as does cheek.

clue.text: Capital character seen in 'Skull Island'

indicators.note: seen in places the word for character inside the word for skull

parts.note: nob is slang for the head or skull
an air is a person's manner or character

explanation.surface: A character appearing in the film Skull Island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skull Island' looks like a film title, but it gives NOB and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital city of Kenya.

clue.text: Last out of newspapers is Times

indicators.note: out of means the letters are taken from inside the run of words

explanation.surface: The last copies left in a stack of newspapers are of the Times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' looks like an adjective but is the verb, meaning go on.
explanation.definitionFit: To persist is to continue or endure, as a thing that lasts does.

clue.text: Abrasion from small clasp retaining middle of bra

indicators.note: retaining means holding, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: a catch is a clasp or fastener

indicators.note: middle of takes the central letter of bra

explanation.surface: A skin graze caused by a little hook on a bra strap.
explanation.definitionFit: A scratch is a shallow mark or graze on the skin, a kind of abrasion.

clue.text: Doctor cut around and deepened cut?

parts.note: to cut around something forms its edge, so edged

explanation.surface: A doctor trimmed round a wound and made the incision deeper.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'cut' is a canal, not an incision, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Dredging a canal deepens it by scooping silt from its bed.
